moments.action: Lynn hurries through a tiled subway corridor thumbing her phone; an insert shows a chat thread filling with coded answer strings, then the cut lands on an extreme close-up of a girl's eyes receiving them.

The other end of the pipeline: a barcode file being edited on a design screen, a hand clicking the mouse, the girl's eyes snapping wide, then a wide of the dim print workshop where one figure works alone at a laptop.
Lynn strides at the camera wiping her face, an insert shows thumbs typing a fresh answer block under messages already marked read, and she walks on with the phone lowered.
A busker plays a keyboard against the station wall; the camera pushes in on his hands, then whips to Lynn passing behind him, glancing back over her shoulder as she keeps moving.
A blurred handoff across a parked motorbike racks into focus as a man in a brown shirt pushes slips of paper into a packed rank of waiting motorcycle-taxi riders, who start pulling away.
Lynn climbs from the lower level, boards an escalator and rides up with her backpack and phone clutched to her chest; by the last shot her eyes are off the screen and fixed ahead.
A train noses into the platform and rushes past the camera; cut to Lynn on the escalator, head up, phone forgotten in her hand as she registers the sound.
A passenger steps aboard carriage N5207 while Lynn bolts down the escalator and sprints along the platform; by the last shot the doors are shut and the train is still.
Lynn stops at the closed door and stares up through the glass, holding there, then tilts her head to the window; the cut answers with a woman's face wide open in a scream.
Shot from behind her, the carriages slide away past Lynn until the platform is bare and other passengers stream by; she turns and walks off under the yellow Way out signs.
An empty escalator shaft, then Lynn rides up in the crowd, steps off at the top and crosses the concourse alone, head down, finally passing a lit perfume billboard.
A platform clock reads 11:19:43 above Lynn's head; she walks past a blue door, and an insert of her hands on the phone cuts to her face screwing up as she reads the screen.

A man in a dark suit comes down the escalator and strides through the station in low-angle shots, intercut with Lynn still frowning at her phone; by the last shot she has turned and is looking back, alarmed.
In the dim workshop a man in a dark shirt hurries to the laptop where a girl in blue school uniform is working; by the end of the take both are hunched over his phone, reading it together.
